correctness.rationale: The formula w_n(k,s)=binom(n,s)A(n−s,k−s) follows by choosing singleton elements. The required Bóna–Mező theorem provides real nonpositive interlacing zeros of nonsingleton-block polynomials P_N; their normalized Poisson-binomial coefficients increase in likelihood-ratio order under increasing Bernoulli parameters. Newton ultra-log-concavity and the Stirling recurrence decompose each normalized adjacent minor into r*a_r^2−(r+1)*a_(r-1)*a_(r+1)+(N−1)*(b_(r−1)*a_r−b_r*a_(r−1)), both nonnegative. Feasible support endpoints shift to the right, so adjacent minors imply all minors even at boundary zeros. Larger K has larger attainable maximal S, yielding strict stochastic order and covariance. Independent exact recurrence checked 81,396 minors for n<=17, but the general claim depends on the analytically read and cited Bóna–Mező interlacing theorem.
